title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — corruptus in Adamo ≠ corruptus simpliciter; root before branches
pass_a_gloss: I set aside his slide from a saying in a certain respect to a saying simply. To be corrupt 'in Adam' with that limit is not the same as to be corrupt without limit. From the former, at the hour when Adam was first corrupted, you get only the root's corruption—not the branches or streams, which were not yet. Being is prior to being corrupt.
pass_b_english: I pass over that the learned man uses the fallacy from what is said in a certain respect to what is said simply. For it is one thing to be corrupt in a certain respect, or with this limitation in Adam, another to be corrupt simply or without such a limitation. This does not follow from that, if the reason of that time is had, when Adam was first corrupted: for the corruption of the root or fountain is signified, not of the branches or streams, because they were not yet. But it is prior to be than to be corrupt.
source_text: Taceo Virum doctum uti fallacia a dicto secundum quid ad dictum simpliciter. Aliud enim est esse corruptum secundum quid, seu cum hac limitatione in Adamo, aliud esse corruptum simpliciter seu absque eiusmodi limitatione. Hoc ex illo non sequitur, si temporis illius ratio habeatur, cum primum Adamus corruptus fuit: significatur enim corruptio radicis seu fontis, non ramorum aut rivorum, quoniam nondum erant: prius autem est esse quam esse corruptum.

choices.choice: secundum quid ≠ simpliciter; root before branches
